note: Rewritten from Snyder's English original of 1924 (AMITERMES BEAUMONTI Banks; the original notes "hitherto unknown winged sexual adults", i.e. the first description of the alate; the soldier was described by Banks). The original gives no measurement table for this caste (none within the window), so no figures are listed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Banks described the species from the soldier, and Snyder (1924) first described its alate. Alate: body brownish black and shining, slightly longer than wide, rounded behind, densely clothed with long pale yellow hairs; fontanelle indistinct, a linear slit in the depression between the compound eyes; antennae 15-segmented, widening towards the apex; compound eyes large, nearly circular, projecting, close against the lateral margins of the head; ocelli long, sunk deeply into the head, their upper margin distinctly overhanging.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body brownish black and shining, slightly longer than wide, rounded behind, densely clothed with long pale yellow hairs. Fontanelle indistinct, a linear slit in the depression between the compound eyes. Antennae dark yellowish brown, 15-segmented, each segment widening towards the apex, clothed with short hairs; segment 1 long, cylindrical; segment 2 shorter (about half of segment 1) and narrower than segment 1, ring-like; segment 3 shorter than segment 2, club-shaped; segment 4 wider than and longer than segment 3; terminal segment narrower, long, nearly oval, pointed at the apex; antennae about as long as the head. Compound eyes black, large, nearly circular, projecting, very close to the lateral margins of the head. Ocelli long, sunk rather deeply into the head (upper margin distinctly overhanging), the distance to the compound eye equal to their short diameter. Labrum yellow, longer than wide, slightly tongue-shaped, narrowing towards the rounded apex, with rather long hairs. Postclypeus pale yellowish brown, inflated, bilobed, less than 2 times as wide as long, posterior margin strongly concave. Pronotum about the same colour as the head, nearly 2 times as wide as long, widest anteriorly, anterior margin concave, posterior margin nearly straight, anterior corners high, sides rounded and converging posteriorly, the whole nearly semicircular, clothed with long hairs. Mesonotum and metanotum paler than the pronotum; mesonotum not covered by the wing scales; posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum angularly concave. Legs pale yellowish brown. Wings dark grey, iridescent, the costal margin darker brown, the wing surface punctate, the margins fringed with hairs; the anal vein running straight to the wing apex, close to the cubitus; the cubitus near the middle of the wing, parallel to the media, with 10—11 branches or subbranches, running straight to the wing apex. Wing scales not as long as the pronotum, clothed with long hairs. Abdomen about the colour of the mesonotum, paler beneath, less than half as long as the wings (dried pinned specimens), densely clothed with long pale yellow hairs.
